public_rationale: The court record supports the ordinary factual core: Anthropic knowingly acquired pirated books before the post, and the court rejected fair use for those central-library copies. The same order found the training use and conversion of purchased print copies lawful. Those distinctions limit the finding but do not erase the documented unauthorized acquisition. Support does not depend on treating the later settlement as an admission.
limitations: Support concerns documented book acquisition, not every creative work or every use.
The order's procedural posture limits claims about final liability.
The broader moral judgment about respecting creators is not independently scored.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic fails to respect the rights of the artists and writers whose work it takes.

statement.excerpt: Anthropic is a business (which incidentally neglects to respect the rights of artist and writers who work they nick).
statement.document_title: New adventures in AI hype: “Our language models are so ‘conscious’ we need to give them rights”

our_interpretation: The plain factual reading is that Anthropic acquired or used creators' protected works in ways that violated their rights.
The statement does not say every work was unlawfully acquired or that every training use infringed copyright.
Unauthorized acquisition is assessed separately from whether subsequent model training is fair use.
The implied past acquisition and use extend through the post date; no starting date is supplied. This is a claim about conduct already undertaken, rather than a periodic financial observation.
Later court records may establish facts about conduct before the post. Settlement alone is not treated as an admission or liability judgment.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish pre-post acquisition or use of protected works without authorization that was not legally excused.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that the challenged acquisition and use were authorized or legally permitted, with no substantiated rights violation remaining.
